title: Moses Argues With God
paragraphs:
Not wildfire.
Not lightning.
Not a mirage bending in the heat.

A bush… burning.
But not consumed.
And standing barefoot before that holy flame was a fugitive shepherd with forty years of failure hanging on his shoulders.
God had just handed him the assignment of a lifetime:

“Go back to Egypt.
Face Pharaoh.
Lead My people out of slavery.”

A nation’s deliverance…
resting on the shoulders of a man who once ran for his life.
And Moses did something that many of us secretly do when God calls.
God answers with miracles in Moses’ own hands — a staff becoming a serpent, a hand turning leprous then clean.

“I’m not the speaking type.”
“I’m awkward.”
“I don’t have the voice.”

“Who made man’s mouth? … Is it not I, the Lord?”
(Exodus 4:11)
The Creator of vocal cords does not need perfect speakers.
Then Moses finally says the thing he was trying to say all along.
And here is the mystery of grace.

He corrects him…
provides Aaron as help…
and still sends him.
Because God's calling is not based on your confidence.
It is based on His covenant.
Yet through that trembling shepherd, God would split a sea, shake an empire, and birth a nation.
The greatest leaders in Scripture did not start with confidence.
But the story whispers something even deeper.
Centuries later, another Deliverer would come who needed none.
Jesus Christ — the greater Moses — would stand before rulers, speak with perfect authority, and deliver His people not from Pharaoh…

At the cross, the Son of God did not say,
“Send someone else.”

And because He obeyed,
our failure can be forgiven.
So if God is stirring something in your heart right now…

A ministry.
A step of faith.
A calling that terrifies you.
God does not call the qualified.

Engagement Question:
Have you ever felt unqualified for something God asked you to do?
Tell your story below. Someone may need the courage hidden inside it.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
